report.source_text: On examination, the best-corrected visual acuity (OD) was 6/24, N8 (−3.50 dioptre sphere, −2.00 dioptre cylindrical, axis 10 degree) and (OS) was 4/60 (-4.00 dioptre sphere, −1.00 dioptre cylindrical, axis 180 degree). Examination with the Amsler grid chart revealed bilateral metamorphopsia. Anterior segment examination of both eyes was normal. She had a clear crystalline lens. The axial length was 24.02 mm (OD) and 24.15 mm (OS). The intraocular pressure was 14 mm Hg in both eyes. Fundoscopic examination revealed full-thickness macular holes in both eyes. The right eye showed a mild temporal peripapillary atrophy. No peripheral retinal breaks were seen. Spectral domain OCT (using the Topcon Maestro 2) was done, which confirmed the presence of FTMHs with cystic spaces in both eyes (figure 1a,b). The minimum inner diameter length of the MH was 431 µm (OD) and 512 µm (OS).

report.source_text: The patient underwent a standard three-port 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy in the left eye first. After core vitrectomy, intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide was injected to stain posterior cortical vitreous and induce posterior vitreous detachment. Air–fluid exchange was done, and ILM was stained with brilliant blue green. ILM peeling was carried out about 2-disc diameters around the macular hole. A non-expansile mixture of 14% C3F8 Gas tamponade was given. The patient was asked to maintain a face-down position for 10 hours a day for 7 days. To minimise the risks associated with bilateral simultaneous surgery, the surgery for the right eye was performed 4 weeks later.

report.source_text: Postoperative visual acuity improved to 6/9 (OD) and 6/18p (OS) after 2 weeks. Fundus examination (OD) showed closure of the macular hole and temporal peripapillary atrophy (figure 2a). OCT (OD) demonstrated type 2A closure of the macular hole with restoration of the foveal contour (figure 2b). Fundus examination also showed closure of the macular hole (figure 2c). OCT (OS) demonstrated type 1B closure of the macular hole (figure 2d).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Bilateral idiopathic macular hole in a young female
clinician.trajectory_summary: A young woman presented with progressive bilateral central vision loss and metamorphopsia over 6 months. Examination revealed reduced visual acuity and fundoscopic confirmation of bilateral full-thickness macular holes. Spectral domain OCT confirmed the presence of macular holes with cystic spaces and measured hole diameters of 431 µm OD and 512 µm OS. No history of trauma, prior surgery, or secondary causes was recorded. The patient underwent sequential pars plana vitrectomy with internal limiting membrane peeling and 14% C3F8 gas tamponade in each eye, followed by face-down positioning. Postoperative evaluation at 2 weeks showed improved visual acuity (6/9 OD and 6/18p OS) and OCT documented type 2A closure OD and type 1B closure OS, confirming successful surgical outcome.
